panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (Left top, Right top, Left bottom, Right bottom). Left top: Fluorescein angiography arterial-phase panel from a 39-year-old man with bilateral Eales disease, showing peripheral nonperfusion and early hyperfluorescence of newly formed vessels. Right top: Capillary-phase fluorescein angiography panel in Eales disease showing sheathed-vessel leakage, new vessels, telangiectasias/microaneurysms, and nonperfusion. Left bottom: Venous-phase fluorescein angiography panel demonstrating sea-fan neovascularization with marked dye leakage in Eales disease. Right bottom: Late-phase fluorescein angiography panel in Eales disease showing leakage from a neovascular membrane and vascular staining.
panels.attribution_text: Călugăru et al. Eales disease in a young adult man Case report.. Romanian journal of ophthalmology 2017. doi:10.22336/rjo.2017.54. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Fluorescein angiography of the right eye in a 39-year-old man with bilateral Eales disease (Left top) The arterial phase shows arterial filling and continuation of the choroidal filling, multiple hypofluorescent laser photocoagulation scars, minimal hyperfluorescence at the area of the newly formed vessels, and well-delineated areas of nonperfusion. (Right top) The arteriovenous (capillary) phase exhibits early laminar flow in veins, leakage of the sheated and newly formed vessels, telangiectasias, microaneurisms, sharply demarcated areas of nonperfusion, hypofluorescence of the photocoagulation scars persists but with slight staining of their margins coming from the adjacent choriocapillaries without leakage of the dye. (Left bottom) The venous phase displays bud-like dilatation of the remaining patent vessels, considerable leakage of the new-formed blood vessels in the form of a sea fan. (Right bottom) The late (elimination) phase demonstrates considerable leakage of the dye coming from the neovascular membrane, remarkable staining of the vessels, increased fluorescence of the photocoagulation foci

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A1, A2, B1, B2). A1: Fundus image of the right eye shows peripheral periphlebitis, a classic Eales disease manifestation. A2: Wide-field fluorescein angiography of the right eye demonstrates peripheral vascular leakage/staining and extensive peripheral capillary non-perfusion consistent with Eales disease. B1: Fundus image of the left eye shows vitreous hemorrhage and neovascularization at the optic disc, typical advanced Eales disease findings. B2: Wide-field fluorescein angiography of the left eye shows 360-degree peripheral retinal capillary non-perfusion and leakage from retinal neovascularization, supporting Eales disease.
panels.attribution_text: Iannetti et al. Cocaine Abuse as an Immunological Trigger in a Case Diagnosed with Eales Disease.. Medicina (Kaunas, Lithuania) 2023. doi:10.3390/medicina59010169. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: In the right eye, fundus imaging (A1) shows peripheral periphlebitis, and wide field fundus fluorescein angiography (A2) shows staining of peripheral vessels as well as areas of retinal capillary nonperfusion with 360-degree peripheral ischemic areas. In the left eye, fundus imaging (B1) shows vitreous hemorrhages as well as retinal neovascularization at the disk area, and in the peripheral retina, wide field fundus fluorescein angiography (B2) shows areas of retinal capillary nonperfusion with 360-degree peripheral ischemic areas as well as areas of leakage from retinal neovascularization.
in_text_mentions: The fundus examination showed signs of peripheral occlusive phlebitis in the BE (Figure 1A1) and partial vitreous hemorrhage with areas of retinal neovascularization in the LE (Figure 1B1). A wide-field fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA) showed delayed venous filling, staining of inflamed peripheral vessel walls in BE, and areas of retinal capillary nonperfusion with 360-degree peripheral ischemic areas in BE (Figure 1A2,B2).

B: Right-eye fundus photo in Eales disease showing pale optic disc, perivascular exudates, hemorrhages, capillary nonperfusion and neovascularization. C: Right-eye fundus photo in Eales disease showing inferotemporal preretinal fibrosis/epiretinal fibrovascular proliferation with retinal tears. D: Right-eye fundus photo in Eales disease showing perivascular exudates, intraretinal hemorrhages, capillary nonperfusion and neovascularization.
panels.attribution_text: Călugăru et al. Eales disease in a young adult man Case report.. Romanian journal of ophthalmology 2017. doi:10.22336/rjo.2017.54. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Ocular fundus of the right eye in a 39-year-old man with bilateral Eales disease. (Left and right top; right bottom) Pallor of the optic nerve head; temporally from the macula in the mid-retina periphery there are scatter wet perivascular exudates, dotted and flame-shaped intraretinal hemorrhages, focal occlusions of retinal vessels, extensive nonperfused areas of the capillaries giving rise to neovascularization; the affected vessels become dilated and tortuous and take on the form of a corkscrew; microaneurysms are observed in the patent capillaries located in the region of a vascular occlusion. (Left bottom) Preretinal fibrosis (epiretinal gliosis) located inferotemporally from the macula in the mid-retina periphery caused retinal tears due to contraction of the fibrovascular tissue

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Fluorescein angiography panel from a case of Eales disease showing arterial-phase non-perfusion, consistent with the captioned manifestation. B: Early venous phase fluorescein angiography in Eales disease demonstrating inflamed vessel staining and optic disc hyperfluorescence/new vessels. C: Fluorescein angiography panel showing peripheral retinal non-perfusion with new vessel formation in Eales disease. D: Late-phase fluorescein angiography in Eales disease showing leakage from new vessels and late vessel staining. E: Fluorescein angiography panel with peripheral retinal non-perfusion and neovascularization in Eales disease. F: Late-phase fluorescein angiography panel showing macular leakage, vessel leakage, and optic disc hyperfluorescence in Eales disease.
panels.attribution_text: Mercuț et al. A Multidisciplinary Approach to the Management of Eales Disease: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.. Journal of personalized medicine 2024. doi:10.3390/jpm14030235. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Fluorescein angiography of the right eye of a 34-year-old male with Eales disease. There were well-delineated areas of non-perfusion in the arterial phase. The early venous phase exhibited staining of the inflamed vessels, hyperfluorescence of the optic disc, and newly formed vessels. We observed leakage at the level of the new vessels and the macula, as well as staining of the vessels during the late phase.
in_text_mentions: Fundus fluorescein angiography was performed for both eyes. The arterial phase revealed sharply demarcated areas of non-perfusion. The early venous phase revealed staining of inflamed veins, well-delineated areas of non-perfusion, and hyperfluorescence of the disc in the area of the newly formed retinal vessels. The late phase demonstrated leakage of the dye from new vessels, significant staining of the vessels, and macular leakage (Figure 3).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (left, right). left: Left panel is an ultra-widefield fundus image from a patient with Eales disease, showing the captioned well-circumscribed peripheral retinal ischemia highlighted by a red box, which corresponds to the Eales disease peripheral capillary non-perfusion finding. right: Right panel is a fluorescein angiogram from the same Eales disease patient, showing the captioned leakage of retinal vessels at the border between perfused and ischemic retina, corresponding to the Eales disease fluorescein leakage finding.

in_text_mentions: At a later date, the patient presented urgently with complaints of blue flashing lights, floaters, and blurry vision in his right eye. A fundoscopic examination and Optos ultra-widefield imaging confirmed a new nasal BRAO in his right eye (Figure 2). Fundus imaging and FA of the left eye demonstrated well-circumscribed areas of ischemia with leakage of retinal vessels at the margin between the perfused and ischemic retina (Figure 3).
